facts.statement: The genus Europelta was described by Kirkland and colleagues in 2013.
facts.quote: authority: Kirkland et al., 2013

facts.statement: Fossils of Europelta were found in the lower Escucha Formation of the Teruel Province in Spain.
facts.quote: in what is now the lower Escucha Formation of the Teruel Province

facts.statement: Two partial skeletons of Europelta were discovered in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, the remains of two partial skeletons of an ankylosaur were discovered

facts.statement: The name Europelta means 'Europe's shield' because it represents the most complete ankylosaur known from Europe.
facts.quote: The generic name, Europelta, combines a contraction for Europe, as it is the most complete ankylosaur from the continent

facts.statement: Europelta was estimated to be 5 meters long and weigh 1.3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Europelta has an estimated length of 5 metres (16 feet) and weight of 1.3 tonnes (2,866 lbs)

facts.statement: Europelta is the largest known member of the dinosaur clade Struthiosaurini.
facts.quote: making it the largest member of the clade Struthiosaurini

facts.statement: The holotype of Europelta includes a mostly complete skull, various vertebrae, ribs, limb bones, and 70 osteoderms.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, AR-1/10, consists of a mostly complete skull, isolated nasals, a dentary fragment, isolated teeth, an atlas, cervical vertebrae, cervical ribs, dorsal vertebrae, a section of synsacrum, isolated dorsal ribs, dorsal rib fragments, caudal vertebrae, chevrons, a coracoid with a small portion of scapula, a scapular blade fragment, xiphosternal plates, partial humeri, an ischium, an ilium, pubes, and 70 osteoderms

facts.statement: The paratype of Europelta consists of a partial jaw, various vertebrae, limb bones, and 90 osteoderms.
facts.quote: The second skeleton that was designated as the paratype specimen, AR-1/31, consists of a partial jaw with dentary and surangular, an isolated angular, teeth, cervical vertebrae, dorsal vertebrae, dorsosacral vertebrae, a sacrum, a caudosacral vertebra, sacral rib fragments, caudal vertebrae, an ilium, ilium fragments, ischia with fused pubes, a femur, a tibia, a fibula, a calcaneum, metatarsals, phalanges, ungual, and 90 osteoderms

facts.statement: Europelta is distinguished by a quadrate bone that is shorter and wider than in any other ankylosaur.
facts.quote: Kirkland and colleagues (2013) diagnosed Europelta based on the quadrate being shorter and mediolaterally wider than in any other ankylosaur

facts.statement: The sacrum of Europelta is arched dorsally by 55 degrees.
facts.quote: the sacrum in lateral view is arched dorsally by 55°

facts.statement: In Europelta, the pubis is fused to the ischium to form an ischiopubis with a slot-shaped opening.
facts.quote: the pubis is fused to the ischium and has a slot-shaped foramen between the post-pubic process and the orientation of the pubic peduncle which forms an ischiopubis

facts.statement: The tibia of Europelta is longer relative to the femur compared to other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: the tibia is longer relative to the length of the femur than in other ankylosaurs

facts.statement: Europelta possesses laterally compressed, flanged osteoderms with a flat base located at the front of the pelvic shield.
facts.quote: the presence of laterally compressed, flanged osteoderms with a flat plate-like base that are present towards the front of the pelvic shield

facts.statement: The skull of Europelta is approximately 370.3 mm long and 299.1 mm wide, narrowing to 203.7 mm at the rear.
facts.quote: The skull has an estimated length of 370.3 mm from the front end of the maxillae to the rear margin of the squamosals and a width of 299.1 mm that narrows to 203.7 mm

facts.statement: The skull of Europelta lacks a distinct post-temporal notch, a feature found in other nodosaurids.
facts.quote: The skull lacks a distinct post-temporal notch, which is a feature seen in polacanthines and other nodosaurids

facts.statement: Europelta had a tooth row with 22 to 25 tooth sockets that grew larger towards the back of the jaw.
facts.quote: The tooth row is arched ventrally and has an estimated 22–25 alveoli that increased in size posteriorly

facts.statement: A suborbital horn in Europelta extends from the quadratojugal bone to the bottom edge of the eye socket.
facts.quote: The suborbital horn is formed mostly from the far end of the quadratojugal to the ventral margin of the orbit

facts.statement: The center of the skull roof of Europelta was covered by a large median scale, similar to other nodosaurids.
facts.quote: The central portion of the skull was covered in an extensive median scale, as in other nodosaurids

facts.statement: Robust scales were present along the edge of the skull, indicated by narrow grooves.
facts.quote: A particular robust pair of scales were present along the margin of the skull based on narrow grooves near the region

facts.statement: The lower jaw bone of Europelta is 184.7 mm long and holds at least 21 tooth positions.
facts.quote: The dentary is 184.7 mm long and preserves a minimum of 21 tooth positions

facts.statement: Europelta's teeth resemble those of Panoplosaurus and Cedarpelta but are less high-crowned than those of other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The teeth of Europelta are similar to the teeth of Panoplosaurus and Cedarpelta but are not as high crowned as in other ankylosaurs

facts.statement: Europelta is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur found in Spain.
facts.quote: Europelta (meaning "Europe's shield") is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from Spain

facts.statement: Europelta represents the most complete ankylosaur fossil known from Europe.
facts.quote: represents the most complete ankylosaur known from Europe

facts.statement: The age of the Europelta fossil site was determined to be early Albian based on microfossil analysis.
facts.quote: The site dates to the early Albian stage of the late Early Cretaceous, based on an analysis of the palynomorphs, ostracods and charophytes (calcareous nannofossils)

facts.statement: Pyrite is commonly found within the bones and bonebed of the Europelta specimens.
facts.quote: The mineral Pyrite is common within the bones and in the bonebeds of the two associated skeletons

facts.statement: Exposure to the surface caused the Europelta bones to degrade, forming a gypsum coating due to pyrite.
facts.quote: When the bones were exposed to the surface, they started to degrade due to the pyrite as indicated by the appearance of fine, powdery to crystalline gypsum coating bones and teeth

facts.statement: The Europelta holotype and paratype are housed at the Funda Museo Aragonés de Paleontología in Spain.
facts.quote: Both specimens are currently housed at the Funda Museo Aragonés de Paleontología, Spain

facts.statement: The species name carbonensis honors the Santa María coal mine where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name, carbonensis, means "from the coal", from the Latin carbo, in honour of the access provided by the Sociedad Anónima Minera Catalano-Aragonesa (SAMCA Group) to the fossil locality where Europelta was found, in the open-pit Santa María coal mine

facts.statement: Europelta possessed amphicoelous vertebrae that were wider than they were tall and constricted in the middle.
facts.quote: The centra of the vertebrae are amphicoelous, wider than tall, are short from front to back, and are constricted in the middle.

facts.statement: Two dorsal vertebrae of Europelta show signs of pathology, characterized by lumpy reactive bone overgrowth.
facts.quote: Two dorsal vertebrae have a centra overgrown by lumpy reactive bone, which appear to be pathological.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that rib fusion in Europelta is an ontogenetic trait because the younger paratype specimen lacks fused ribs.
facts.quote: The paratype specimen doesn't preserve any fused ribs which suggests that this character is ontogenetic as the paratype represents a smaller and presumably younger individual than the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Unlike other ankylosaurs, the sacrum of Europelta is strongly arched from front to back.
facts.quote: Unlike other ankylosaur sacra, the sacrum of Europelta is strongly arched from the front to the back.

facts.statement: The last four caudal vertebrae and their chevrons in Europelta are fused into a tapering terminal rod at the tail's end.
facts.quote: The most distal four caudal vertebrae and their chevrons are fused together which form a tapering, terminal rod of bone at the end of the tail.

facts.statement: Europelta represents the oldest known ankylosaur to preserve a straight ischium.
facts.quote: Europelta preserves as straight ischium and represents the oldest ankylosaur with such characteristic.

facts.statement: The paratype specimen of Europelta preserves a calcaneum, a bone practically unknown in ankylosaurs except in Niobrarasaurus and juvenile Anodontosaurus.
facts.quote: The paratype specimen preserves a calcaneum which is practically unknown in ankylosaurs except for Niobrarasaurus and a juvenile specimen of Anodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Like other nodosaurids, Europelta had a foot with four pedal phalanges.
facts.quote: As in other nodosaurids, Europelta possessed a pes with four pedal phalanges.

facts.statement: The claw-like unguals of Europelta are spade-shaped and morphologically similar to those of other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The unguals are spade-like and share a similar morphology to the pedal unguals in other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype and paratype specimens of Europelta were found with abundant osteoderms, but these were not preserved in their original positions relative to the skeleton.
facts.quote: Both the holotype and paratype specimen of Europelta were preserved with an abundance of osteoderms but weren't preserved in situ with any of the skeletal elements or with each other.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Europelta have a moderately rough texture with sparse pitting, similar to those of nodosaurids and basal ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of Europelta have a moderately rugose texture with sparse pitting as in nodosaurids and basal ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: Small, variably shaped ossicles likely filled the gaps between the larger osteoderms on Europelta.
facts.quote: Small ossicles that ranged in shape probably filled in the spaces between larger osteoderms.

facts.statement: Large, similarly sized osteoderms on the posterior ilium of Europelta are tightly sutured but not coossified, unlike in Aletopelta.
facts.quote: The posterior margin of the ilium preserves large, subequal-sized osteoderms that are tightly sutured together but was not coossified as in Aletopelta.

facts.statement: The femoral head of Europelta is angled at approximately 115 degrees relative to the femur's long axis.
facts.quote: The femoral head has an articular surface directed dorsally and forms an angle of about 115° with the long axis of the femur.

facts.statement: The tibia of Europelta features a broadly rounded cnemial crest.
facts.quote: The tibia preserves a cnemial crest that is broadly rounded.

facts.statement: Hollow, plate-like osteoderms with sharp edges ran down the sides of Europelta's tail and decreased in size rapidly.
facts.quote: Osteoderms with sharp anterior and posterior edges, and are hollow, asymmetric-based plate-like ran down the sides of the tail but decreased in size more rapidly.

facts.statement: Fossils of Europelta were found in the lower zone of the Escucha Formation in Teruel province, northeastern Spain.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se encontraron en la zona inferior de la Formación Escucha de la provincia de Teruel, en el noreste de España.

facts.statement: The animal is known from two associated partial skeletons, representing the most complete fossil record of a European ankylosaur.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de dos esqueletos parciales asociados, que representan el material fósil más completo conocido de un anquilosaurio de Europa.

facts.statement: Europelta lived during the mid-Cretaceous, specifically the early Albian stage, approximately 113 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del Cretácico, a inicios del Albiense, hace 113 millones de años

facts.statement: Europelta was a medium-sized nodosaurid measuring approximately 4.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Europelta es un nodosáurido de tamaño mediano, aproximadamente de 4,5 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The posterior margin of the skull is concave when viewed from above.
facts.quote: El margen posterior del cráneo es cóncavo en vista dorsal.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Europelta arches dorsally by nearly 55 degrees.
facts.quote: El sacro de Europelta se arquea dorsalmente en cerca de 55°.

facts.statement: The pubis fuses completely with the ischium to create a notch-shaped foramen between the postpubic process and the pubic peduncle, forming an ischiopubis.
facts.quote: El pubis se fusiona por completo al isquion, creando un foramen en forma de muesca entre el proceso postpúbico y la posición del pedúnculo púbico formando un isquiopubis.

facts.statement: The ratio of tibia to femur length is 0.9, which is higher than in other ankylosaurs for which these proportions are known.
facts.quote: La proporción de las longitudes de tibia a fémur, que es de 0.9, es mayor que en otros anquilosaurios para los cuales estas proporciones son conocidas.

facts.statement: The skull is pear-shaped from above, measuring 370.3 mm in length and 299.1 mm in width above the eye sockets.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene forma de pera en la vista superior, con una longitud de 370,3 milímetros y un ancho, sobre las cuencas de los ojos, de 299,1 milímetros.

facts.statement: The last six teeth at the rear are notably larger than the front teeth.
facts.quote: Los últimos seis dientes en la parte trasera son notablemente más grandes que los dientes delanteros.

facts.statement: Scaly horns are present at the rear corners of the skull.
facts.quote: En las esquinas traseras del cráneo hay cuernos escamosos.

facts.statement: The large cheek horn is formed by the quadratojugal bone rather than the jugal bone.
facts.quote: El cuerno de la mejilla grande está formado por el cuadratojugal en lugar del hueso yugal.

facts.statement: The genus Europelta was named by Kirkland et al. in 2013.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Kirkland et al., 2013

facts.statement: The species Europelta carbonensis was named by Kirkland et al. in 2013.
facts.quote: species_authority: Kirkland et al., 2013

facts.statement: Europelta is classified within the subfamily Struthiosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Struthiosaurinae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Europelta belongs to Struthiosaurinae, as the original classification lacked a phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Kirkland et al. (2013) originally classified Europelta as a member of Struthiosaurinae but did not conduct a phylogenetic analysis to determine its exact relationships within the clade.

facts.statement: Researchers disagree on Europelta's closest relatives, with some studies placing it as sister to Pawpawsaurus and others including Borealopelta in that relationship.
facts.quote: Arbour et al. (2016) placed Europelta as sister taxon to Pawpawsaurus, while Brown et al. (2017) recovered it as sister taxon to both Pawpawsaurus and Borealopelta.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses place Europelta in a polytomy with Struthiosaurus, Stegopelta, Hungarosaurus, and Pawpawsaurus.
facts.quote: Zheng et al. (2018) recovered it in a polytomy with Struthiosaurus, Stegopelta, Hungarosaurus and Pawpawsaurus.

facts.statement: Other studies suggest Europelta is the sister taxon to Hungarosaurus.
facts.quote: Rivera-Sylva et al. (2018) placed Europelta as sister taxon to Hungarosaurus.

facts.statement: Microfossils indicate that the habitat was a permanent freshwater lake.
facts.quote: The microfossil assemblage of the member exclusively consists of freshwater ostracods and charophytes which suggests that the member was a permanent lacustrine.

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing layer consists of dark olive-gray to olive-black mudstone preserving a high percentage of fossil plant debris.
facts.quote: The layer that the holotype and paratype specimens of Europelta were obtained from have a characteristic dark olive-gray to olive-black mudstone that preserves a high percentage of fossil plant debris.

facts.statement: Evidence of fused fern lamellae and abundant charcoal indicates the area was affected by a wildfire.
facts.quote: The presence of fused lamella in charred remains of ferns and the presence of abundant macro- and meso-charcoal remains together with a great amount of micro-charcoal indicates that the assemblage was affected by a wildfire.

facts.statement: Heavy rainfall likely moved charred remains downstream where they were later buried in a nearby depositional area.
facts.quote: The combination of the properties of the burnt soil and the action of heavy rainfalls suggests the charred remains moved downstream and were buried later in a near depositional area.

facts.statement: The genus Europelta was originally described and named by James I. Kirkland, Luis Alcalá, Mark A. Loewen, Eduardo Espílez, Luis Mampel, and Jelle P. Wiersma in 2013.
facts.quote: Europelta fue descrito y nombrado originalmente por James I. Kirkland, Luis Alcalá, Mark A. Loewen, Eduardo Espílez, Luis Mampel y Jelle P. Wiersma en 2013

facts.statement: The genus name combines a contraction of "Europe" because it is the most complete ankylosaur from the continent and the Greek word "pelta" meaning "shield".
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina una contracción de Europa, ya que este es el anquilosaurio más completo del continente, y el término πέλτα, pelta, del griego antiguo para "escudo"

facts.statement: The species name means "of coal" in Greek, honoring the access provided by the mining company SAMCA at the Santa María open-pit coal mine where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie significa "del carbón" en griego, en agradecimiento al acceso provisto por la Sociedad Anónima Minera Catalano-Aragonesa, Grupo SAMCA, a la localidad fósil en donde se halló a Europelta, en la mina de carbón a cielo abierto de Santa María

facts.statement: Europelta is known from two associated partial skeletons deposited at the Teruel-Dinópolis Paleontological Collection Foundation/Museum of Aragon Paleontology.
facts.quote: Europelta es conocido a partir de dos esqueletos parciales asociados, depositados en la Fundación Conjunto Paleontológico de Teruel-Dinópolis/Museo Aragonés de Paleontología

facts.statement: The site dates to the early Albian stage, based on an analysis of palynomorphs, ostracods, and carophytes (nanofossils).
facts.quote: El sitio data de inicios del Albiense, basándose en un análisis de los palinomorfos, ostrácodos y carofitos (nanofósiles)
